summary: This bill amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow businesses to immediately deduct up to $20,000 in start-up and organizational expenditures, with the remaining amount amortized over 180 months, and prevents the loss of net operating loss carryforwards and tax credits for new businesses after an ownership change.

scores.thoughts: This bill amends the Internal Revenue Code to simplify and expand deductions for start-up and organizational expenditures, and to preserve net operating losses and tax credits for start-up businesses after an ownership change. These changes generally reduce the tax burden for eligible new businesses, thus lowering taxes.

The bill expands immediate tax deductions for startup and organizational expenses and shields startup NOLs/credits from post-ownership-change limitations. Both changes reduce federal revenue relative to current law, increasing the deficit to support new-business formation. The entire bill consists of these targeted tax expenditures, but the legislation frames itself as an innovation measure rather than a fiscal or deficit bill, making the deficit impact real yet secondary.
